I see therapy (particularly cognitive-behavioral therapy) as ultimately reliant on deluding patients. Now, delusion is not always a bad thing. If someone believes good things about themselves, they get the tangible and very real benefits of high self-esteem and maybe they ride the high well enough to actually succeed in something that is real.

The main strategy for therapists is to convince you to recognize positive things in life, which will make you feel good and stabilize your mood. Now, if someone actually has positive things, then that makes the therapists job way easier. But, what if their life actually sucks?
